dictionary.definition: color, tint, hue, shade; beauty, form; sex

etymology.hint: What a person ⺈ desires 巴

currentComponents.note: ⺈ (a person, bent over) — the figure whose outward expression is being depicted.
巴 — traditionally linked to desire or emotion, so together the character points to a person's expression or complexion, extended to 色's meaning 'color, appearance.'

dictionary.definition: to grant, to consent; just, fair
to get, to obtain, to receive, to sieze

usedInWords.meaning: variant of 收穫|收获[shou1 huo4]

currentComponents.note: 艹 (grass) — 获 relates to harvesting crops from the field.
又 (a hand) — a hand grasping and gathering, reinforcing 获's meaning 'to obtain, to harvest, to gain.'

dictionary.definition: to strike, to hit, to beat; to attack, to fight

etymology.hint: Simplified form of 擊; 手 provides the meaning

currentComponents.note: 手 (hand) — in the traditional form 擊, 手 contributed the meaning of striking with force, the source of 击's meaning 'to hit, strike.'

dictionary.definition: to exhaust, to use up, to deplete

currentComponents.note: 皿 (a vessel or dish) — 尽 relates to using up everything inside, to the last drop.
Above the vessel, strokes depicting a hand with a brush scrape the dish clean, giving 尽 its meaning 'to exhaust, to the utmost, to the end.'

etymology.hint: Using a tool 殳 to sort items on a tray 舟

currentComponents.note: 舟 (boat/tray) — represents a vessel or tray holding items.
殳 (a hand with a tool) — sorting or moving items on a tray gave 般 its meaning 'sort, kind, manner.'

etymology.hint: The smaller 小 brother

currentComponents.note: 小 (small, young) — 叔 describes a younger member of the family.
又 (a hand) — historically part of a scene of picking beans; today it simply combines with 小 to give 叔 its meaning 'a younger uncle.'

etymology.hint: a poisonous plant

currentComponents.note: 龶 depicts a poisonous plant, tying 毒 to its meaning 'poison.'
母 (mǔ) gives a rhyme close to dú, with the initial shifted.

etymology.hint: fire

currentComponents.note: 火 (fire) — linked to ritual fires once used to try to communicate with spirits
彐 (jì) gives a sound distantly related to 灵's reading líng, having drifted apart considerably over time

dictionary.definition: to appoint, to commission, to send

currentComponents.note: 禾 (a grain stalk, bending under its own weight) sits above 女.
女 (woman) below suggests a yielding, pliant posture — together evoking something entrusted or handed over, the root of 委's meaning "to entrust, to delegate."

dictionary.definition: to fill, to supply; to be full

currentComponents.note: 充 is built on 儿 (a person) at its base, with the upper strokes tracing a child growing tall. This image of steady growth gave 充 its meaning 'to fill, to be full, sufficient.'

etymology.hint: A home 广 with a servant 隶

currentComponents.note: 广 depicts a simple roofed building, a home.
隶 depicts a servant or laborer — a household with help was traditionally a sign of ease and well-being, giving 康 its meaning 'healthy, peaceful.'

dictionary.definition: the future, what will be; ready, prepared; a general

etymology.hint: Going to bed 丬 at night 夕, a predictable future

currentComponents.note: 丬 (a stylized bed) — 将 originally pictured someone preparing for bed at night.
夕 (evening/night) — the coming of night was seen as predictable, giving 将 its meaning 'about to' or 'going to' happen.

dictionary.definition: business, profession; to study, to work

currentComponents.note: 业 (simplified from 業) depicts a wooden board with a jagged, saw-tooth top edge, once used to hang bells and chime-stones for ceremonial music. The idea of a fixed set of tasks tied to that ritual work broadened over time into 业's modern meaning, 'occupation, industry, achievement.'

dictionary.definition: and; with; to; for; to give, to grant

usedInWords.meaning: (idiom) to stand out from the crowd

currentComponents.note: 与's ancient form pictured two hands jointly lifting or offering an object — an image of giving or participating together, which gave 与 its meanings 'and, with, to give.'

etymology.hint: A great 大 celebration in a house 广

currentComponents.note: 广 (a building/shelter) — the setting of the celebration.
大 (great, big) — a grand event held inside, together giving 庆 its meaning 'to celebrate.'

dictionary.definition: to open, to unfold; to extend, to stretch

etymology.hint: Laying out clothes 㠭 for sale in a market 尸; compare 㠭

currentComponents.note: 尸 (here representing a covering or stall, not a corpse) — 展 pictures a place where goods are displayed.
衣 (clothing) — clothing laid out for display gave 展 its meaning 'to unfold' or 'to exhibit.'

dictionary.definition: more, further; to shift, to alternate; to modify
to spare, to excuse from; to evade

currentComponents.note: 免 began as a pictograph closely related to 兔 (rabbit) with its tail dropped — a hare slipping free of danger gave 免 its meanings 'to escape, to avoid, to be exempt from.'

etymology.hint: ear

currentComponents.note: 耳 (ear) — the original meaning of 耶 is unrelated to its modern use, which is mainly phonetic.
阝 (a place-name element) gives a sound distantly related to yé, having drifted apart over time.

etymology.hint: grain

currentComponents.note: 禾 (grain) — 稣 was originally tied to reviving or gathering grain.
鱼 (yú) gives a sound only distantly related to sū today, having drifted apart over time.
尢 (yóu) gives the sound — an exact match with 尤's reading yóu.

dictionary.definition: bold, brave; to dare, to venture

etymology.hint: A hand with a stick 攵 striking a beast 耳

currentComponents.note: 耳 — a wild beast being confronted
攵 (a hand with a stick) — striking at the beast, showing boldness

dictionary.definition: ruler, tape-measure; unit of length, about 1 ft.

etymology.hint: Picture of a man measuring by pacing

usedInWords.meaning: foot (unit of length equal to 0.3048 m)

currentComponents.note: 尺 is traditionally read as a picture of a bent leg taking a measured step, used before rulers existed to pace off a distance — the origin of its meaning 'a Chinese foot, a ruler.'

dictionary.definition: to cease, to finish, to stop, to quit

etymology.hint: Stuck in a net 罒, unable to leave 去

usedInWords.meaning: a modal particle indicating resignation or acceptance

currentComponents.note: 罒 (a net) — something trapped inside it.
去 (to leave, go) — unable to get away, together giving 罢 its meaning 'to stop, cease.'

etymology.hint: A child 儿 in a room with four walls 囗

currentComponents.note: 囗 (an enclosure) — 四 pictures a bounded space.
儿 (a person) — a person enclosed within four walls gave 四 its meaning 'four,' though the exact link to the number is debated.

etymology.hint: A person 夭 on stilts

currentComponents.note: 夭 depicts a person leaning to one side, arms swinging — here the pose of walking high up on stilts, giving 乔 its meaning 'tall, lofty.'
黍 (millet grain) appears in 黎's upper portion, tying the character to fields of crops and, by extension, the multitude of common people (黎民) who worked them.
灬 (fire/light) at the base evokes a first glow of light, fitting 黎's use in 黎明 'dawn, daybreak.'

etymology.hint: Two arrows 丨 pulled across a bow

currentComponents.note: 弓 (a bow) — the curved frame.
丨 (a straight line), shown twice — arrows or a bowstring pulled tight across it; the character is mostly used today in transliteration.

etymology.hint: bright

currentComponents.note: 冏 (bright, a window admitting light) — appears in 商's ancient form, though its exact link to 'commerce, to discuss' is unclear today.
章 — a graphic element whose original contribution to the character's meaning has been lost over time.

尔 is a simplified, cursive-derived form of the traditional 爾, whose ancient shape depicted an ornamental woven lattice or window pattern; that concrete image was later dropped as the character was borrowed to write the pronoun 'you, that' and, in transliterations, the syllable ěr.

dictionary.definition: to guard, to protect, to defend

currentComponents.note: 卫 is a simplified form of 衛, which originally pictured feet marching around a bounded area, soldiers patrolling the perimeter of a settlement, the source of its meaning 'to guard, to defend.'

dictionary.definition: summer; the Xia or Hsia dynasty

currentComponents.note: Ancient forms show a person wearing an elaborate mask or headdress, thought to depict a ceremonial dancer performing summer rain-and-harvest rituals — the origin of 夏's meaning 'summer' and, by extension, the name of China's first dynasty.

The traditional form 亂 showed a hand at each end of a tangled skein of thread on a spool, an image of trying to sort out a disordered mess. The simplified 乱 keeps only a trace of that hand-and-thread arrangement, but retains the meaning 'chaotic, in disorder.'

etymology.hint: Five elements (the cross with the extra stroke) between heaven 一 and earth 一

currentComponents.note: 五 places an X-shaped cross between two horizontal lines representing heaven and earth — in traditional cosmology, this was linked to the five elements that fill the space between.

etymology.hint: A place where measures 尺 are discussed 口

usedInWords.meaning: (of a batter) to be put out (in baseball)

currentComponents.note: 尺 (a ruler/measure) — represents rules or measures being set.
口 (mouth) — measures being discussed aloud in one place gave 局 its meaning 'bureau, office, situation.'

An ancient pictograph of a claw-like hand with bent fingers; it was later adopted as the name of the second earthly branch (associated with the ox) and, separately, as a simplified stand-in for 醜, 'ugly.'

dictionary.definition: to advance; to arise; to hoist, to raise

usedInWords.meaning: to go up by one grade

currentComponents.note: 升 is a pictograph of an ancient grain-measuring ladle or vessel. Scooping and lifting grain with it gave rise to the extended meaning 'to rise, to ascend,' and the character also survives today as a unit of volume equal to one liter.

dictionary.definition: to resist, to bear; patient, enduring

etymology.hint: A man 大 wrapped in a long 镸 cloth

currentComponents.note: 大 (big, a person with arms and legs spread) pictures a person.
镸 (long) pictures a long piece of cloth wrapped around them, giving 套 its meaning 'cover, case.'

etymology.hint: A jade statue 王 with four holes made in it 口

currentComponents.note: The repeated 口 (mouth) shapes are thought to represent cries of alarm or distress, tying into the character's meaning of 'shocking, ill-omened.'

usedInWords.meaning: Long live (the king, the revolution etc)!

currentComponents.note: The upper part of 岁 preserves a fragment of 步 (to walk, to step) from the traditional form 歲, hinting at time passing step by step.
夕 (evening) — one evening following another built up the sense of a full year passing, and by extension, a person's age.

dictionary.definition: to advance; to increase; to promote

etymology.hint: An advance to the second 亚 day 日

currentComponents.note: 亚 (here a stylized shape related to advancing in rank) sits above.
日 (sun, day) below anchors the meaning in time, giving 晋 its sense 'to advance, to promote.'

肃 is the simplified form of 肅, which pictured a hand grasping a tool and working with tight, careful concentration over an intricate pattern. The focus and self-restraint that scene called for carried over into 肃's meaning: 'solemn, respectful, stern.'

The oracle-bone form of 六 pictured a simple hut or shelter with a peaked roof; that picture was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the number six, and the original 'shelter' meaning was dropped entirely.

etymology.hint: A hand 彐 threshing rice

currentComponents.note: A hand shape.
Represents grain being handled, linked to labor and servitude.

乡 is a simplified form of the traditional 鄉, whose ancient shape showed two people kneeling on either side of a shared food vessel — a picture of a community eating together — which gave 鄉/乡 its meaning 'village, hometown, countryside.'
